name: event-iowa-lead-azide
title: The US Army blew up its lead azide stockpile. Who would pay if it went wrong?
sub: About 5 tons of degraded explosive were detonated at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant after a court cleared it. EPA monitors detected no airborne lead.
rowsTitle: Where insurance would feel it if lead dust spread
rows: It largely self-insures. Claims against it run through the Federal Tort Claims Act, not an insurer.
Contamination and clean-up are typically excluded from home and farm policies.
General liability usually excludes pollution; it needs specialist pollution or environmental cover.
The long-tail route: exposure and medical-monitoring claims can surface years later.
verdict: Read today: little insured loss. No lead detected and an all-clear given. Watch soil tests and any lawsuits.
caption:
The US Army detonated its entire stockpile of lead azide, about 5 tons, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on 25 November, after a court cleared the way. EPA monitors detected no airborne lead and FEMA issued an all-clear.

If lead dust had spread, who would pay?
🏛️ The government largely self-insures: claims go through the Federal Tort Claims Act
🏡 Home and farm policies typically exclude contamination and clean-up
🏗️ Contractors need specialist pollution cover; standard liability usually excludes it
⚖️ Toxic tort claims are the long tail to watch

For now: little insured impact. The things to watch are soil test results and whether lawsuits follow.
